task.description: The page has a heading #course-title, a paragraph #lesson-count and a list of lessons li.lesson with .lesson__name and .lesson__status inside. jQuery is already loaded. 1) Write the text "jQuery in 10 lessons" into #course-title and add the class is-ready in the same chain. 2) Save the number of lessons in the constant lessonCount using .length. 3) Write the text "Lessons on the page: 4" into #lesson-count, where the number is lessonCount. 4) With one call, write the text "not started" into all .lesson__status elements. 5) Read the heading text into the constant titleText and print it to the console. Do not use document.querySelector, innerHTML or .html().

tests.name: The heading has the class is-ready
The heading text and class are set in one chain
On a page with five lessons, lessonCount equals 5
tests.fail: Do not write the number by hand - take it from $(".lesson").length.

tests.name: All lessons have the status "not started"
tests.fail: $(".lesson__status").text("not started"); - one call changes all elements.

tests.name: titleText is the heading text
tests.fail: Read the text after changing it: const titleText = $("#course-title").text();

tests.name: titleText is printed to the console
The code is written with jQuery
tests.fail: No loops and no textContent: $(".lesson").length and $(".lesson__status").text(...).

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: Check the selectors and make sure the .text() getter is not in the middle of a chain.

hints: One call $(".lesson__status").text("not started") changes all statuses.
Read titleText after you have changed the heading.

questions.question: What is jQuery?
options: A separate programming language that replaces JavaScript
A JavaScript library with ready-made functions for working with the page
questions.explanation: jQuery is an ordinary .js file. Inside, it calls the same DOM functions as plain JavaScript.

questions.question: Which loading order is correct?
options: jQuery is loaded at the end of body after main.js
questions.explanation: Scripts run in order: without jQuery loaded, main.js has no $ function.

questions.question: What does $(".card") return if there are no cards on the page?
options: An empty jQuery object with length 0
questions.explanation: $() always returns a jQuery object. Check: $(".card").length === 0.

questions.question: Which property of a jQuery object shows how many elements were found?
questions.explanation: $(".item").length is the number of elements found.

questions.question: What does $(".status").text("Done") do if the page has 3 .status elements?
options: Throws an error: a loop is needed
questions.explanation: Implicit iteration: a setter is applied to each element that was found.

questions.question: Match the code with the result.
questions.explanation: A getter returns a value, a setter returns a jQuery object for chaining, and [0] returns a DOM element.

questions.question: Which chains will work without an error?
questions.explanation: You can continue a chain after a setter. The .text() getter returns a string, and length is a number.

questions.question: What will the user see after $("#msg").text("Hello")?
questions.explanation: .text() inserts a string as text, not as markup - like textContent.

questions.question: Which code runs after the DOM is built and is recommended in jQuery 4?
questions.explanation: $(function) is the recommended form; $(document).ready is deprecated.

questions.question: What is missing from the slim build of jQuery?
questions.explanation: Slim is lighter because it has no effects and no AJAX. The course uses the full build.

questions.question: What do you type in the console to find out the version of the loaded jQuery? Enter the whole expression.
questions.explanation: jQuery.fn.jquery returns the version string, for example "4.1.0".

questions.question: Match plain JavaScript code with jQuery code.
pairs: A DOM element from a jQuery object
questions.explanation: jQuery does the same things as the browser's DOM functions, but in less code.
